_listing: Artosia's page in the Microsoft Store. Artosia is a free program for a church's media desk: it puts the words of songs, Bible verses and announcements on the projector during a service. It runs on a Windows 10 or 11 computer. The reader is a church volunteer of any age who searched the Store or was sent the link, and decides in a few seconds whether this is what the church needs. Register: plain, modest and concrete, the way a friendly program speaks in your language; say what the thing is and does, then stop. No exclamation mark, no em-dash, no en-dash, no middle dot, no emoji, no word such as best, powerful, seamless or ultimate, and no promise the facts below do not make. Sentence case. Program names (Artosia, EasiSlides, OpenLyrics, PowerPoint, Windows, Wi-Fi, GPL-3.0-or-later) stay as written. Names of things inside the program are the words you chose for its window (Design, Screens, Announcements, the plan, Preview and Live, the phone remote). The Store shows plain text: no markup, a blank line between paragraphs.
_facts: Shows song words, Bible verses and announcements on a projector or any second screen; the operator's window stays on the first screen.
Finds a song by its title or by any line of its words, forgives typing mistakes, and shows the matching line.
Finds a Bible passage by its reference or by its words. Bibles are downloaded from free collections, each showing its own copyright line first, or opened from a church's own file.
A plan for each service: songs, passages and announcements in order. Preview shows what comes next and Live shows what the room sees; nothing reaches the projector until Show is pressed.
Design: the text's size, place and font, over a colour, a picture, a looping video or a live camera. A gallery of free backdrops is built in.
A second window for the band's own screen shows the words, what comes next and a clock.
A remote on a phone over the church's Wi-Fi, joined with a four-digit code: next and back, sections of the song, the plan, search, a message to the room, a countdown.
Announcement and birthday cards loop before the service.
It can listen to the room through a microphone and offer the song being sung; the speech is read on the computer itself and nothing is sent anywhere.
It can send the projector's picture to a live stream with the church's own stream address and key.
It brings in songs from EasiSlides and from OpenLyrics files, and words pasted from anywhere.
Free, with no account, no advertising and nothing collected. Open source under GPL-3.0-or-later.
The window speaks ten languages: Indonesian, English, Chinese (simplified and traditional), Korean, Japanese, Spanish, Portuguese, French and Vietnamese.
The church's library is kept in the Documents folder, in a folder named Artosia, so it stays when the program is removed.
